title: Superb AI Raises About $10 Million in Pre-IPO Funding Ahead of Planned 2026 IPO
summary: Executive Summary Hanwha Asset Management’s venture fund, POSCO Investment, and other major investors participated in the round. Cumulative funding now totals K
body_text: Announcements Superb AI Raises About $10 Million in Pre-IPO Funding Ahead of Planned 2026 IPO Hyun Kim Co-Founder & CEO | 2025/12/15 | 10 min read Linkedin X(twitter) Executive Summary Hanwha Asset Management’s venture fund, POSCO Investment, and other major investors participated in the round. Cumulative funding now totals KRW 63 billion (about $43 million), underscoring the proven value of Superb AI’s solutions across real-world industrial environments in steel, manufacturing, logistics, defense, and more. New capital will be dedicated to advancing AI technology and expanding globally, with the goal of accelerating AI adoption across industries. Superb AI, an all-in-one vision AI solution provider, announced on the 15th that it has closed a KRW 14 billion (approximately $10 million) pre-IPO (pre-initial public offering) equity funding round. The round was joined by Hanwha Asset Management’s venture fund, POSCO Investment, and other major investors, bringing Superb AI’s total funding to KRW 63 billion (approximately $43 million) as it targets a 2026 stock market listing. Since earlier funding rounds, Superb AI has attracted investment from leading Korean conglomerate affiliates—including Doosan, Hyundai Motor, Samsung Electronics, KT, Kakao, KT&G, and HL Group—validating the company’s technical capabilities. Many of these strategic investors have since become major customers, an uncommon case in which existing customers or potential customers invest not only for financial returns but also for the synergies created by adopting AI solutions. These companies are actively using Superb AI’s solutions across their own industrial environments, such as manufacturing and logistics. In particular, collaborations with Hyundai Motor and Doosan have accelerated following their investments and are now translating into tangible business results. Superb AI specializes in vision AI technologies that analyze and recognize images, videos, and 3D LiDAR data. Since its founding, the company has built a data-centric AI development approach grounded in the belief that the essence of AI lies in data quality. Through its flagship Superb Platform—an end-to-end system that automates everything from data construction to model training—the company enables users to develop AI with minimal friction. Superb AI also launched ZERO, Korea’s first industrial vision foundation model for real-world environments, and has demonstrated its technical strength by winning awards in global benchmarks and competitions. ZERO is a general-purpose AI model that can be applied to diverse visual tasks without extensive additional training and is recognized for significantly lowering AI adoption barriers by delivering high performance with relatively small amounts of data. Superb AI has also been selected as one of the “K-AI Companies,” a group developing national AI models that represent Korea, and is participating in the Ministry of Science and ICT’s national AI foundation model project as part of an LG AI Research–led consortium. As the only non-LG affiliate responsible for foundation model development, Superb AI is leveraging the core technologies behind ZERO to lead the construction of multimodal data for physical AI. The company currently operates entities in Korea, the United States, and Japan, and provides vision AI solutions to more than 100 enterprise customers worldwide, including Samsung, LG, Hyundai Motor, and KT. Its Japanese subsidiary, established last year, has grown rapidly, adding leading manufacturers such as Toyota and Nippon Steel as customers. Superb AI recently renewed its contract with Toyota and continues to expand its partnership with Nippon Steel, its first customer in the Japanese market. The company is also extending its customer base in Japan to include national research institutes and major consumer electronics manufacturers. Superb AI’s technological capabilities are also recognized through global partnerships. The company was named AWS Rising Star Partner of the Year last year, and, through a close partnership with NVIDIA, is deepening technical collaboration in video surveillance systems (VSS) while jointly delivering AI projects across global industrial sites—further solidifying its position as a technology leader. With the proceeds from this round, Superb AI plans to invest aggressively in advancing its AI technologies and attracting top talent, while expanding sales to large domestic enterprises, their affiliates, and a wide range of industries that are seeking to adopt AI. The company also intends to accelerate its global market expansion to secure new growth drivers. Superb AI and its key investors aim to go beyond simple technology adoption, pursuing joint growth by co-developing technologies and projects, and commercializing solutions through sales and distribution partnerships. A representative from the Hanwha Asset Management venture fund, which led this round, commented, “Superb AI’s vision AI technology can be applied across a wide range of industries, including manufacturing, aerospace, foodtech, shipbuilding, and defense.” Superb AI has won the Hanwha Systems AI Challenge for two consecutive years, underscoring the strength of its technology. A representative from POSCO Investment, which also participated as a major investor, said, “We began as a customer of Superb AI and were able to validate the effectiveness of its solutions. Based on that, we evaluated the company’s technical strength and growth potential and decided to invest. Superb AI has the execution capability to deliver results across a variety of environments, including manufacturing, logistics, and safety monitoring.” “It is especially meaningful that this funding round comes from leading industrial partners who first worked with us as customers,” said Hyun Kim, CEO of Superb AI. “By deepening our collaboration with these partners, we aim to accelerate AI adoption across industries and, through our planned IPO in 2026, take the next step toward becoming a global leader in the industrial AI market.” (End) - Superb AI: An All-in-One Solution Provider Supporting Every Stage of Vision AI Adoption Founded in 2018, Superb AI is an MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) startup that supports the full lifecycle of AI development. The company provides a wide range of products and services that help enterprises build and successfully deploy AI systems. Its solutions enable customers to construct a complete, iterative MLOps pipeline—from dataset creation, selection, processing, management, and analysis through to model training, deployment, and continuous improvement. From the outset, Superb AI has focused on supporting enterprises adopting vision AI based on images, video, and 3D LiDAR data. Its intuitive tools allow even users without coding or machine learning expertise to develop and manage AI, with a user experience streamlined enough to build deep learning models in just a few clicks. In 2025, Superb AI launched Superb AI Video Analytics, a video-based AI solution that detects anomalies—such as fires, falls, and intrusions—in real time across large numbers of CCTV feeds, while also providing text-based intelligent search. Powered by multimodal AI and Visual Language Models (VLMs), the solution delivers higher accuracy and greater usability than traditional video monitoring systems, enabling advanced automation for smart cities, industrial sites, logistics facilities, and public institutions. The same year, the company introduced its vision foundation model ZERO, recognized as Korea’s first practical AI model designed for direct deployment in industrial environments. ZERO allows users to perform desired tasks using only text prompts or example images, without the need for complex coding or deep ML expertise, and incorporates “zero-shot” capabilities to flexibly handle new environments without extensive pre-training. Superb AI delivers AI solutions to more than 100 enterprise customers worldwide, including leading technology companies such as Toyota, KT, Samsung, LG Electronics, Qualcomm, Hyundai Motor, and SK Telecom. The company operates entities in Korea, the United States, and Japan as it continues to expand its global footprint. To date, Superb AI has raised approximately 63 billion Korean won (around 43 million USD) from investors in Korea and the U.S. and is pursuing an IPO with a target listing in 2026. The company has obtained SOC 2 Type II certification, demonstrating its adherence to rigorous global security and operational standards. Within just one month of its founding, Superb AI filed its first domestic patent, and it has since registered a total of 26 patents in the United States, Japan, and Korea related to the auto-labeling and custom auto-labeling capabilities of Superb Platform and its AI development pipeline. Superb AI offers Superb Platform, a high-performance AI development platform that supports the entire AI lifecycle on a single system, and Superb Service, through which the company’s experts provide end-to-end support—from consulting and data design to AI algorithm development and operations. In addition, Superb AI offers vertical AI solutions tailored to industrial sites, including Superb AI Video Analytics, Superb AI Defect Detection, and Superb AI Edge, which can be delivered in combination according to customer needs. title: Clinically Relevant 3D Tumor Models for HER2-Targeted ADC Development
summary: Expanding the Preclinical Toolbox with a Novel Patient-Derived Organoid Platform
body_text: Expanding the Preclinical Toolbox with a Novel Patient-Derived Organoid Platform The human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) plays a central role in regulating cell growth, division, and survival. When overexpressed, it acts as an "on switch", driving accelerated cell growth and uncontrolled tumor spread. This biology underlies the aggressive behavior observed in HER2-positive cancers, which is associated with higher recurrence rates and poorer patient outcomes. While genomic changes in HER2 are most frequently discussed in the context of breast cancer, HER2 alterations are also found in non-small cell lung, ovarian, colorectal, and pancreatic cancers. HER2-Targeted ADCs in Cancer Therapy HER2-targeted therapies have significantly changed the treatment landscape and brought new hope and better outcomes for patients. Among them, HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have emerged as a particularly promising approach, combining the specificity of antibodies with the potency of cytotoxic payloads. These agents enable targeted delivery directly to HER2-expressing tumor cells while limiting off-target toxicity. FDA approved drugs in this class include trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1, Kadcyla®) and trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd, Enhertu®), both of which have demonstrated meaningful clinical responses (Figure 1). A growing number of next-generation HER2 ADCs are now in development. Figure 1. FDA approved HER2-targeted ADCs trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1, Kadcyla®) and trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd, Enhertu®). Figure adapted from Joubert et al1. As ADCs become an increasingly important therapeutic modality, the limitations of conventional preclinical models have become magnified. Drug developers need better, more physiologically relevant and predictive preclinical models to support ADC development, ones capable of reproducing tumor architecture, heterogeneity, and treatment response. Limitations of Traditional 2D Preclinical Models for ADC Evaluation Despite their widespread use, traditional 2D cell culture models have well-recognized drawbacks with respect to evaluating targeted therapies. They often fail to capture key biological features of tumors and inadequately replicate the complex tumor microenvironment (TME) that influences drug response in patients. Target accessibility, receptor density, internalization kinetics, and payload penetration are all influenced by three-dimensional tumor structure, features which are largely absent in 2D cultures. As a result, 2D assays may overestimate drug potency or fail to distinguish on-target activity from nonspecific cytotoxicity, reducing their predictive value for clinical translation. In contrast, growing tumor cells as 3D organoids allows for a spatially organized structure that more closely resembles the in vivo microenvironment and architecture of patient tumors. Champions has developed a scalable 3D screening platform based on HER2-positive patient-derived xenograft organoids (PDXOs). Derived from well-characterized PDX models, our ex vivo 3D organoids maintain clinically translatable HER2 expression, providing a relevant and predictive platform for evaluating the efficacy of HER2-targeted ADCs. Validation of HER2-Positive PDXO Models HER2-positive ex vivo PDXO breast cancer models generated from our TumorGraft3D (CTG-3D) platform were evaluated for HER2 expression as well as functional responses to the clinically approved HER2-targeted ADCs, trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) and trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-Dxd). The workflow is shown in Figure 2. Figure 2. Workflow overview to evaluate HER2-targeted ADCs using breast cancer PDXO models. HER2 Expression Immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PDXO tissue blocks demonstrated complete and intense membrane staining (HER2 score 3+) across HER2-positive models. Consistent with these findings, flow cytometric analysis of enzyme-dissociated organoids identified HER2-positivity in 61.8% to 90.1% of cells. In contrast, the HER2-negative control PDXO model showed no detectable HER2 staining by IHC and negligible HER2 expression by flow cytometry, confirming assay specificity and the absence of nonspecific background signal. A subset of the results is shown in Figure 3. Figure 3. HER2 expression assessed by IHC and flow cytometry analysis. A) HER2-positive PDXO and B) HER2-negative PDXO model. Together, the IHC staining and flow cytometry results are consistent with the clinical annotation and indicate that HER2 expression is maintained relatively homogeneously in breast cancer PDXO models. Response to HER2-Targeted ADCs After confirmation of HER2 expression, the PDXO models were evaluated for their response to two clinically approved HER2-targeted ADCs, trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) and trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1). Both ADCs were tested against HER2-positive and HER2-negative breast cancer PDXOs and reference breast cancer cell lines. In addition to intact ADCs, corresponding cytotoxic payloads (Exatecan and DM1), naked antibody (trastuzumab), and—for T-DXd—an isotype-payload conjugate (IgG-DXd) were evaluated to distinguish potency, selectivity, and target-dependent activity. Drug response was measured using the CellTiter-Glo® viability assay following six days of incubation with the ADCs and control treatments. Figure 4. Representative dose-response curves (IC₅₀). A) HER2-positive PDXO model comparing exatecan (payload) and trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) and B) control naked antibody trastuzumab and isotype-payload conjugate IgG-DXd. Across HER2-positive breast cancer PDXO models and control cell lines, ADCs demonstrated greater efficacy and specificity compared with naked antibody and isotype-payload controls (Figure 4, and data not shown). Full datasets across additional PDXO models are presented in the accompanying AACR 2025 poster . These results highlight the utility of PDXO models derived from Champions’ CTG-3D platform for evaluating next-generation ADCs and discriminating between payload-driven cytotoxicity, nonspecific conjugate effects, and HER2-targeted ADC activity. To further quantify differential treatment responses, normalized Area Under the Curve (∆AUC) values were calculated to capture response differences between isotype controls and ADCs across the full concentration range. HER2-positive breast cancer cell lines and PDXO models exhibited higher ∆AUC values (approximately 30–50%, data not shown), indicating stronger ADC activity relative to controls. In contrast, HER2-negative models showed substantially lower ∆AUC values (~20%), consistent with reduced ADC activity in the absence of target expression (Figure 5). Figure 5. Normalized ∆AUC. The response difference between isotypes and ADCs is calculated as: [AUC of Isotype] – [AUC of ADC] / [AUC of Isotype ] x 100% Collectively, these findings demonstrate that breast cancer PDXO models generated from Champions’ CTG-3D platform reproduce expected response patterns to FDA-approved HER2-targeted ADCs with known pharmacological profiles, supporting their utility as a predictive ex vivo platform for ADC development. Key Takeaways Champions’ CTG-3D platform is a biologically relevant ex vivo 3D platform that can support critical preclinical decisions, including payload comparison and mechanism-based screening, enabling ADC candidates to be screened and prioritized before more expensive in vivo evaluation and clinical development is undertaken. For drug developers, this translates into greater confidence in candidate selection, improved translational relevance of preclinical data, and reduced risk of late-stage attrition of potentially viable candidates. By enabling better-informed decisions earlier in the development process, the CTG-3D platform helps accelerate the advancement of safer and more effective ADC-based therapies. To explore the full datasets in more detail, download the full poster presented at AACR 2025 here. References Joubert, Nicolas, Alain Beck, Charles Dumontet, and Caroline Denevault-Sabourin. 2020. “Antibody-Drug Conjugates: The Last Decade.” Pharmaceuticals (Basel, Switzerland) 13 (9). https://doi.org/10.3390/ph13090245 .

title: British Airways selects RTX's Pratt & Whitney GTF™ engines to power up to 63 Airbus A320neo aircraft
summary: UK flag carrier opts for game-changing geared architecture LONDON, July 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Farnborough International Airshow – Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, announced today that British Airways has selected GTF engines to power 33 firm and 30 option Airbus A320neo aircraft. Pratt & Whitney will also provide maintenance for the engines through a 12-year EngineWise®Comprehensive services agreement, ensuring optimized fleet efficiency and cost of ownership. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2027.
body_text: British Airways selects RTX's Pratt & Whitney GTF™ engines to power up to 63 Airbus A320neo aircraft July 20, 2026 Share this article on Facebook Share this article on Twitter Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article via email UK flag carrier opts for game-changing geared architecture LONDON , July 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Farnborough International Airshow – Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, announced today that British Airways has selected GTF engines to power 33 firm and 30 option Airbus A320neo aircraft. Pratt & Whitney will also provide maintenance for the engines through a 12-year EngineWise® Comprehensive services agreement, ensuring optimized fleet efficiency and cost of ownership. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2027. "Today marks a pivotal moment and a strong vote of confidence in the GTF engine as the UK's flagship carrier, British Airways, becomes the newest GTF customer," said Rick Deurloo, president of Commercial Engines, Pratt & Whitney. "As the most fuel-efficient choice for the A320neo aircraft, the GTF engine will help British Airways achieve its international fleet expansion goals and enhance the travel experience for passengers." British Airways currently operates a fleet of IAE V2500-powered A320ceo family aircraft. The GTF delivers 20% lower fuel consumption and a 75% smaller noise footprint compared to the prior generation of engines. Over 2,800 GTF-powered aircraft are operated globally by more than 90 customers, and the order backlog of over 8,000 GTF engines reflects strong market demand for its proven benefits. The GTF Advantage engine, which will enter into service later this year, will provide operators up to twice the time on wing, industry-leading fuel efficiency and even more range capability. About Pratt & Whitney Pratt & Whitney, an RTX business, is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power units for military, commercial and civil aviation customers. Since 1925, our engineers have pioneered the development of revolutionary aircraft propulsion technologies, and today we support more than 90,000 in-service engines through our global network of maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities. About RTX With more than 180,000 global employees, RTX pushes the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia For questions or to schedule an interview, please contact [email protected] SOURCE RTX Tags : RTX Pratt ＆ Whitney Airshow Press Release If you like this article, share it. title: FDA Approves Gwyn Lo Birth Control Patch: A New Low-Dose Weekly Contraceptive Option for Women
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Gwyn Lo, a new once-weekly hormonal contraceptive patch designed to provide women with another convenient and reversible birth control option. body_text: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Gwyn Lo, a new once-weekly hormonal contraceptive patch designed to provide women with another convenient and reversible birth control option. Developed by Viatris Inc., Gwyn Lo combines two hormones, norelgestromin and ethinyl estradiol, in a low-dose estrogen patch intended for women who are suitable candidates for combined hormonal contraception. The approval represents a new development in women’s health by expanding contraceptive choices beyond daily pills, implants, injections, and intrauterine devices. With its once-weekly application schedule, Gwyn Lo may appeal to women who prefer a non-invasive method that does not require daily medication reminders. What Is Gwyn Lo Birth Control Patch? Gwyn Lo is a combined hormonal contraceptive (CHC) patch that delivers norelgestromin 220 mcg per day and ethinyl estradiol 20 mcg per day through the skin. The patch is designed to release hormones steadily during each seven-day wear period. The contraceptive patch follows a weekly schedule. Users apply one patch each week for three consecutive weeks, followed by one patch-free week. This schedule is intended to provide pregnancy prevention while reducing the need for daily contraceptive management. The FDA approval applies to women of childbearing potential with a body mass index (BMI) below 30 kg/m² who are appropriate candidates for combined hormonal contraception. Why the Approval of Gwyn Lo Matters Access to a wide range of contraceptive options is important because women have different health needs, lifestyles, and preferences. Some women prefer methods that require daily attention, while others seek longer-lasting or lower-maintenance options. Unintended pregnancy continues to be a significant public health concern in the United States. According to referenced national health data, unintended pregnancies represented a substantial portion of pregnancies in recent years. Research has also shown that many women change or discontinue contraceptive methods because they experience concerns, side effects, or dissatisfaction with their current option. Gwyn Lo provides another choice for women looking for a reversible, non-invasive contraceptive method with a low estrogen dose. Clinical Trial Results Supporting FDA Approval The FDA approval of Gwyn Lo was supported by results from the Phase 3 Luminous Study, a clinical trial evaluating contraceptive effectiveness, safety, and patch performance. The study measured contraceptive effectiveness using the Pearl Index, which estimates the number of pregnancies occurring per 100 woman-years of exposure. Among women included in the efficacy evaluation group, the Pearl Index was reported as 4.14 with a 95% confidence interval of 2.77 to 5.95. Researchers also evaluated how well the patch remained attached during everyday activities. During the year-long study, 39,790 patches were applied, and only 1.3% completely detached. This finding demonstrated strong patch adhesion performance under real-world conditions. The study also monitored common side effects. Reported adverse reactions occurring in at least 2% of participants included: • Application site irritation • Skin redness at the application area • Application site itching • Bleeding between menstrual cycles • Heavy withdrawal bleeding • Nausea Researchers observed improvements in cycle control over time. Rates of unscheduled bleeding or spotting decreased from 34.5% during the first cycle to 20% by cycle 13. The average duration of these episodes also declined. How Does Gwyn Lo Work? Gwyn Lo works by releasing synthetic versions of estrogen and progestin hormones through the skin. These hormones help prevent pregnancy primarily by stopping ovulation. They may also change cervical mucus, making it more difficult for sperm to reach an egg, and alter the uterine lining. The patch uses a multilayer matrix design. The active ingredients and adhesive are contained within a flexible structure that supports controlled hormone delivery throughout the seven-day application period. Additional Phase 1 studies evaluated patch performance under different conditions, including exercise, sauna exposure, whirlpool use, and cold-water bathing. These studies showed consistent hormone delivery across different environments. Important Safety Information About Gwyn Lo Like other combined hormonal contraceptives, Gwyn Lo may not be suitable for everyone. Women should discuss their medical history and individual risk factors with a healthcare provider before starting this medication. The FDA labeling states that Gwyn Lo is contraindicated for women who smoke and are over 35 years old because of an increased risk of serious cardiovascular events. The product is also contraindicated for women with a BMI of 30 kg/m² or higher. Women should seek medical advice before using any hormonal contraceptive, especially if they have a history of blood clots, cardiovascular conditions, certain cancers, liver problems, or other medical concerns. Availability of Gwyn Lo Viatris announced that Gwyn Lo is expected to become commercially available later in the year following FDA approval. The company stated that the product reflects its continued focus on developing healthcare solutions, including innovations in women’s health. The introduction of Gwyn Lo adds another option to the growing range of contraceptive methods available to women in the United States. The Future of Contraceptive Options The approval of new contraceptive technologies highlights the continued demand for flexible and personalized reproductive healthcare choices. While some women prefer long-acting methods, others may value methods that offer control, convenience, and easy discontinuation. Weekly contraceptive patches like Gwyn Lo may provide an alternative for women who want the effectiveness of hormonal contraception without taking a daily pill. As healthcare providers and patients continue discussing contraceptive options, access to accurate information remains essential for making informed decisions. Conclusion The FDA approval of Gwyn Lo marks an important step in expanding available birth control choices for eligible women. As a once-weekly, low-dose estrogen contraceptive patch, Gwyn Lo offers a convenient and reversible option for women seeking an alternative to daily contraceptive methods. Although the patch provides a new option, choosing a contraceptive method should always involve a discussion with a qualified healthcare professional. Individual health history, lifestyle, and personal preferences all play an important role in selecting the most appropriate method. Sources Viatris Inc. Individual results and suitability may vary depending on personal health conditions and medical history.

title: DuPont launches ultrafiltration modules with integrated pre-filter
summary: DuPont today announced the launch of Inge™ ultrafiltration modules with integrated pre-filter (iP-F).
body_text: WILMINGTON, Del., April 7, 2026 — DuPont (NYSE: DD) today announced the launch of Inge™ ultrafiltration modules with integrated pre-filter (iP-F). Where conventional ultrafiltration plant processes require a separate pre-filtration manifold to remove debris and particulates, the integrated pre-filter offering combines pre-filtration and ultrafiltration into a single module housing—which can help reduce plant footprint and the associated capital and operational costs of standalone pre-filtration units. The new product line maintains the same membrane materials, dimensions, and drinking water certifications as existing Inge™ UF modules, while combining two filtration steps into one. Inge™ UF modules with iP-F are well suited for new installations, plant expansions, and containerized systems where space efficiency and streamlined operations are critical. “By combining pre-filtration and ultrafiltration into a single unit operation, Inge™ ultrafiltration modules with integrated pre-filter will help customers simplify plant design while protecting their UF membrane investment,” said Dorie Yontz, Global Marketing Leader, Drinking Water & Desalination at DuPont Water Solutions. “The result is a more compact, efficient solution that supports reliable performance across a range of water qualities.” Inge™ UF modules with iP‑F can provide consistent permeate quality, pathogen removal, and tolerance to feedwater quality swings—all in a smaller footprint than conventional media filters and traditional UF plant designs with upstream prefilters. System performance and design scenarios can be evaluated using DuPont’s WAVE PRO modeling software, helping customers assess treatment configurations as part of the overall process design. DuPont Water Solutions technologies are helping to purify more than 50 million gallons of water every minute in 112 countries across the world. DuPont offers market-leading technologies to address a variety of challenges faced by water treatment municipalities, seawater desalination plants, and industrial water users, including the microelectronics industry, through a broad portfolio of membranes, resins and complete systems. The team is also innovating solutions that can help balance the world’s growing water and energy demands, with products that support the production of electricity, lithium and green hydrogen.

title: In-depth Guide for How to Ace your Product Hunt Launch 😻
summary: How we became the #1 Product of the day, week, and month on Product Hunt🏆
body_text: Me celebrating SigmaOS becoming the #1 Product of the Day As a product geek, there is really only one place to find new tech products. The brainchild of Ryan Hoover, with the logo of a cat wearing a google lens, Product Hunt! Like many startup founders, designers, and product geeks, I lurk Product Hunt daily to find new cool productivity tools or SaaS products I can use. I even found Notion when they initially launched there as an easy way to create wikis for your company. 🤓 So I always wanted to launch my own startup’s product on Product Hunt, where people could discover and geek out over it. When the time came a year ago to finally release SigmaOS on Product hunt as part of our launch schedule from YCombinator, I was super nervous. Ok, maybe not nervous, but more like freaking out that nobody would care about our launch , and we would barely even get 100 upvotes. Now you can imagine my surprise when the day came, and we kept getting upvotes. But it didn't stop just there; Product Hunt and Fast Company wrote an article about us which brought more upvotes, and we became #1 product of the day . I was blown away when it all didn't stop there. The following week came around, and SigmaOS became #1 product of the week . Before I knew it, SigmaOS was #1 product of the month and the year ended with us being nominated as a semi-finalist for Product of the Year 🤯 After SigmaOS's launch, I've got 100s of emails and Twitter DMs asking from founders, product developers, and indie hackers about how they can launch on Product Hunt to get the best results . So I thought to write this to explain what we did and some hacks we used for our launch; apparently, it worked 😂 Create a timeline, and focus on it 📆 Breaking down your launch into a three-part timeline like a month before, a week before, and the day of launch will help you hit your goals 🤩. Alright, first things first, planning. You need to plan what your expectations are as an outcome for your Product Hunt launch before you actually start doing preparations and work on it. Make sure to set yourself the goal you want, whether it is the #1 product of the day or a certain amount of downloads, and optimize everything you do until your launch day for that goal only. 📆 The next thing to do is create a timeline for yourself. To get the best results, you should give yourself about a month of preparations so you can make sure you have built up everything for your launch, whether it is your landing page, product, subscriber base, or list of people who will upvote you (more on that later). What we did for SigmaOS was to break our timeline into three timestamps; a month before your launch, a week before your launch, and the day of your launch. This way, you can track what you need to do at every step to make sure you'll hit the goal you have set for your launch. 🏆 Create a checklist on Notion ✅ Create a homepage on Notion to have a checklist of everything you need to get done before launch day 📝. So this part is pretty straightforward but super crucial to making sure nothing falls through the cracks and you succeed. On your startup's notion workspace, create a "Product Hunt Launch Checklist" page and invite anyone in your team who will be working on your launch. At the top, put the launch day, so everyone has it right in front of them (time pressure-induced anxiety from time to time has never hurt anyone 😅). Next, you want to put your objectives and key results from those objectives so everyone is pushing in the same direction; for example, what we wanted for SigmaOS's launch was #1 Product of the day. As a key result, we wanted 500 early users. Now add your timeline and the to-dos you need to do during those timelines. ☑️ You can download SigmaOS and add the exact Product Hunt workspace template my cofounders and I used throughout our Product Hunt prep and launch; you'll get the notion board we used to stay on track, plus the perfect setup leading up to your launch and the launch day. 🖥 Set up a Ship page 🛳 Product Hunt's Ship is an excellent initial place to start talking about your upcoming launch publicly and get early traction for it 🚀. To get some early sign-ups and awareness for your launch on Product Hunt, creating an upcoming page on Product Hunt through Ship is excellent. This will allow you to build directly a subscriber list of people who are Product Hunt users and who are active followers on the platform. People who subscribe to your page can even share your page directly through Twitter, so you can get further visibility for your launch and retweet all those tweets from your new subscribers. Lastly, having an upcoming page will let you beat the drum to your launch consistently leading up to your launch day and get you further visibility on Product Hunt itself. 😻 SigmaOS's Ship page on Product Hunt Next, you want to do two more things for your upcoming page, add the link to your page to all of your social media accounts and integrate ProductHunt into a channel on your Slack . 🔌 SigmaOS's Ship dashboard on Product Hunt Join maker, founder, and indie hacker communities 🕺🏻 To have a successful launch, you need to engage with many startup communities , especially the individuals and influencers in those communities 🌟. Alright, you've set up your timeline and upcoming page, time to join some communities of like-minded people who can help you on launch day. The first community you should join is Product Hunt's makers community . This is a community of fellow product nerds constantly launching and talking about the new cool products being launched. So, join the discussion, share your milestones, upvote other Makers' milestones, follow makers, comment on makers' discussions, and cheer other Makers' launches; good karma always comes back in many folds. 😇 Next, start joining some Slack communities focused on startup founders, indie hackers, and product nerds. Remember when you join those communities not to only promote your own product, nobody likes an entrepreneur who joins to only promote their stuff 🙄. Have someone from your team actually engage with those communities, answer questions, participate in the conversation, ask for advice, and keep them posted on your progress (Trust me, they also like to see you succeed). In our "Product Hunt Launch Checklist" notion page in the SigmaOS Product Hunt launch workspace template, you'll find a list of all the Slack communities we found super valuable to join! 🤩 Get template for free 🌟 Create a list of people who will upvote you 🔺 Creating a list of potential upvotes will give you a lot of headspace on launch day, and you need to make sure to have at least 2x the number of people on your list the upvotes you want to get ⏫. It is important to start keeping track of people who can upvote you after joining all those communities on your launch day. The best way to do this is to create a table on Airtable or Notion to make sure you can also add extra properties to each person, like on which community you talked to them and how likely it is for them to upvote you if you messaged them on the day. But don't stop there increasing your list. Shortlist people in your network that are influencers or have a healthy following. You can even add people who have upvoted and commented on similar products to yours on Product Hunt to your list and follow them, so you are on their radar. What day and time is the best to launch? 🤔 Getting first is hard but staying first is easy if you launch at the right time and get your initial influx of upvotes then 💯. The best time to launch on Product Hunt is at 12:05am PT ; launching at this time makes sure you are on the trending section and are visible throughout the day. Now, depending on what you are trying to go for, i.e., #1 Product of the week or #1 Product of the month, we found that launching the first or second week of the month on Wednesday gets you the best amount of traffic and sets you up on track to hit those goals as well. Finding your Hunter 👀 A top hunter for your product can make a big difference, and you can find one in communities like Makers . Now that you have done all your planning and setup, it is time to find a hunter to hunt your product launch on Product Hunt. A great hunter who has hunted similar products to yours can really help you get a consistent influx of upvotes during your launch day. But finding a hunter could be a bit daunting or outright intimidating. So, first things first, look amongst your own community members to see if there is someone who can hunt you or, even better, introduce you to a hunter who you think would be perfect for your startup. Alternatively, you can find makers and hunters who are very active on the Product Hunt on Makers . Makers have a list of top 500 hunters ranked by the number of upvotes they've gotten for products they have hunted. Create your media kit for your launch 📸 A good media kit can make your launch stand out and the life of your hunter easier 🎬. So after you have found your hunter, you need to help them help you. One of the key ways to do this is to create your media kit for your startup’s launch that they can use to set up your launch page and schedule your launch. A complete media kit for your launch that your hunter can use needs to have the following: Product name A mistake we made in our launch was not using a keyword like "browser" in our product name, so make sure not to make the same mistake. 🥲 URL (has to be a new URL if you've posted to Product Hunt before) Tagline (under 60 characters) Make your tagline exciting and catchy, so it grabs attention; we made ours about the user "A browser that makes YOU fast" to differentiate ourselves from every other similar product on the platform. 😉 Description (under 260 characters) You want to make this super short and to the point. We did this with a one-liner that describes what the product does and who it is for, followed by the top 3 functionalities our users love, and ended with our call to action. PH profile URL of the makers Company Twitter handle Share if this product is "free," "paid," or "paid with a free trial or plan." Topics (you can choose 3–4 topics for your product) Media, including screenshots, images, logos. (You should include a thumbnail image. Thumbnails are displayed as a square. Avoid text if possible. Recommended size: 600 x 600px or bigger. If you are uploading a GIF, ensure it is under 3MB.) make sure to label the photos based on the order you'd like them to appear on PH. GIF thumbnails always work the best; again, you want to grab attention between all the other products being launched that day There is a massive debate about using images or videos for your launch page. We went for images because they are a lot easier to produce, you are still a founder and have a hell of a lot of work, and people don't really want to sit through a 2-5 minute video. Get them on your page, make them understand what you offer asap, and get them to try your new product so they upvote it! Date/time you'd like your product submitted. Beat the drum rolling up to the launch day 🥁 You need to keep beating the drum of your Product Hunt launch up to the day of the launch, so you stay on everyone's mind and keep growing your following 📣. Send updates consistently to your subscribers, waitlist, and early adopters about your launch once a week . People love hearing updates and feel like they are part of the journey, so stay on their radar throughout the building up to your launch. Your updates can also ask people to become beta testers or tell them about a cool way one of your users has been using your new product; the update doesn't have to be just about Product Hunt. The big day is tomorrow 🤩 Make sure you have your setup for the day ready and get plenty of rest 🛌. The Product Hunt launch is tomorrow, so there are a few small but very important things you need to do. First, send another update telling all your subscribers that you are launching tomorrow. Second, make sure you are all set up . Have these pages locked and loaded: Mention → Keep track of conversations and product mentions across all channels. Product wars 2 → Track how your product is performing on the daily rankings Notify → Know when someone says something about your company/industry etc. Customer.io → Send an email to your community on launch day informing them of your launch. I made sure I had a specific workspace on SigmaOS before the launch day and loaded all my pages. This helped me respond to everything happening on the day, and ensure nothing would fall through the cracks. If you'd like to make it super easy for yourself and get the same setup as I did on SigmaOS's launch day, you can just get my workspace set up on SigmaOS. SigmaOS's launch page on Product Hunt Last but not least, get some rest . Tomorrow is gonna be a crazy long day for you, and you need to be performing at your best! What to do on the big day? 📣 When your product is launched, jump in the comments , post your intro message , respond to all comments , tweets, or mentions online, and keep messaging people from your list and community 🎙. As soon as your product is submitted, you should jump into the thread and introduce yourself as the maker. Briefly introduce yourself, the team, and the problem you're solving. In 3-4 sentences, explain the value prop, the use case, who it's for, and why you're building it. If this is the second time you're launching on Product Hunt (i.e., a big product update or huge feature announcement), explain what's changed. Make sure to write and edit your intro comment pre-launch. It is sending an update to subscribers time 💌. Let them all know you have launched on Product Hunt and you are live so they can upvote you . Now you need to make sure to get to 100 upvotes within the first hour of your launch; time to whip out that beautiful list you prepped beforehand and message the 200 most likely people who will upvote you (some might be asleep since your launch will be super early or late 😅). Jump into the comments and respond to any comments anyone posts ASAP. But Product Hunt isn't the only place people might be talking about your launch, announce it on all your social media platforms, especially LinkedIn and Twitter , and check if someone has posted about it and like, comment, and share ASAP. And for the rest of the day, you need to keep the influx of upvotes coming. So continue hustling within the communities you joined and contacting people from your Airtable list. Your Product Hunt launch has finished; what's next? 😮‍💨 When your launch is over, keep building on top of the momentum by posting and writing about it 🥳. The launch is done, and you probably have hit your goals, but the work isn't done yet . After your launch is over, you need to send the last update email to your subscribers and new users. Tell them about your success and thank them for helping you get there; continue building your karma and good standing since this won't be the last time you'll launch on Product Hunt. And lastly, build upon the launch hype , write a blog about your experience to continue the kindle of your launch burning. (maybe not months later like I did 😅)

title: Roblox Expands Teen Council for Civility and Well-Being to South America
summary: Applications Now Open Across Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, and the U.S.
body_text: Share Safety + Civility Community Roblox Expands Teen Council for Civility and Well-Being to South America Applications Now Open Across Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, and the U.S. By Tami Bhaumik, Vice President of Civility and Partnerships Published Jul 21, 2026 As Roblox’s user base expands and fast-paced high-fidelity games attract more teens and young adults, meeting their needs means bringing their voices into the room. That’s why we launched our first Teen Council in 2024. With 80% of Roblox’s player community outside the U.S., engaging young people in new parts of the world brings authentic insight into cultural needs. And helps our safety efforts and product features resonate locally while empowering the next generation of digital well-being advocates. This year’s Teen Council for Civility and Well-Being is expanding to include teens from Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Peru—in addition to Canada, Mexico, and the U.S. Users aged 13 to 17 can apply here for the next council, which runs from October 2026 to June 2027. Applications are open now through midnight PDT on August 18. We also announced our inaugural Asia Pacific Teen Council earlier this year and continue seeking applicants from Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia. “Our products, as well as our safety and well-being initiatives, are stronger and more authentic when they’re shaped by the voices of our players,” said Andres Cuervo, Roblox’s Senior Program Manager for Youth Engagement. “We’re looking for young leaders, especially those who are passionate about digital well-being, to bring their insights to the table and help us continue to be a global leader in online safety and civility.” Teen Council’s Impact The 2026 Teen Council brought together 20 users, aged 14 to 17, from across North America. Members provided input on features like Roblox Kids and Roblox Select accounts and new chat tools, engaging with Roblox leadership across safety, marketing, and engineering. The council helped develop a youth guide to Roblox’s Community Standards —written in plain language to help younger users understand platform rules. We used that same language to simplify our in-game reporting flow . Members also collaborated with media literacy organizations on Roblox’s second digital well-being public service announcement and a new youth well-being page for Mental Health Awareness Month . Teen Council members collaborated with media literacy organizations on a digital well-being public service announcement. “Serving on the council proved how influential teen insight can be when we’re given a seat at the table,” said Sofia, a 2026 Teen Council member. “Roblox really made space for us to feel empowered as advocates and problem-solvers.” “Every meeting, we heard from new Roblox team members eager to hear our feedback on their work—and then we got to see just how much our feedback impacted the final launch,” said council member Maggie. How to Apply Users aged 13 to 17 living in Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, or the U.S. can now apply here for Roblox’s 2027 Teen Council. Applicants for the Asia Pacific council can apply here . All candidates must be proficient English speakers and have parental consent to apply. Applications must be received by midnight PDT on August 18.

title: How to Fly to Asia with Points: Business Class for Less
summary: Learn how to fly to Asia in business class with points: which transfer partners unlock ANA and Star Alliance seats, what they cost, and how to book.
body_text: How to Fly to Asia with Points: Business Class for Less A round-trip business class seat to Asia routinely sells for $5,000 to $8,000 or more in cash. That same lie-flat seat, on the same plane, can book for around 105,000 to 120,000 points round-trip. The cheapest single-program path starts at just 60,000 miles one-way. Most travelers never see those numbers because they only search cash fares. A transpacific business class fare is often the single most expensive line item on a trip, which is exactly why booking it with points erases the most money. The hard part is not the flight. It is knowing which airline to transfer to, what a fair price looks like, and how to find a seat that is actually open. This guide covers all of it: which transfer partners unlock Asia business class, what a seat realistically costs in points, when award space opens, and how to book one step by step. Pointhound searches award availability across 200+ airlines and 21 loyalty programs, so you can see which Asia flights your existing points can book, and at what value, before you transfer anything. Why Use Points to Fly Business Class to Asia? Using points for business class to Asia means transferring credit card rewards to an airline program and booking an award seat, which is worth far more than redeeming the same points for cash through a card portal. Here is the core gap. Your credit card portal gives you about 1 to 1.5 cents per point. Transfer those same points to an airline and they can be worth 2 to 20 times that. The multiplier climbs with the cabin: roughly 10 times the portal value in business class and up to 20 times in first class. Asia is where the gap gets dramatic. Premium transpacific cash fares are among the highest a regular traveler will ever see, so a points booking wipes out thousands of dollars in one move. And award bookings can sometimes earn miles, depending on the program, so a points ticket is not always a dead end for future travel. Sample one-way business seat Cash price Points cost Value per point U.S. West Coast to Tokyo (ANA via Virgin Atlantic) ~$2,800 52,500 points ~5.3 cents U.S. to Asia on Star Alliance (Turkish) ~$2,800 60,000 miles ~4.7 cents U.S. West Coast to Singapore (Singapore Airlines) ~$3,000 112,500 miles ~2.7 cents A common worry stops people before they start: "I'll never have enough points for business class." In practice, a single welcome bonus on a mainstream travel card often lands you 60,000 points or more, and two of them can cover a round-trip lie-flat seat across the Pacific. You do not need years of spending. You need to know where the points go furthest. Which Credit Card Points Can You Use for Asia Business Class? Five transferable points programs feed airline travel to Asia: Chase Ultimate Rewards, American Express Membership Rewards, Capital One miles, Citi ThankYou Rewards, and Bilt Rewards. Each moves points into airline programs, mostly at a 1-to-1 ratio. You do not fly on "Chase" or "Amex." You transfer those points into an airline loyalty program, then book the airline's seat. That one distinction trips up almost every beginner, and it is the entire game. Every cardholder has at least one strong path. Chase and Amex reach the widest set of programs, while Capital One, Citi, and Bilt each feed at least two of the programs below. Most transfers are instant. The one slow exception to plan around is American Express to ANA, which takes two to four business days to land, according to ANA . If your points sit with Amex, our Amex Membership Rewards guide covers every partner in detail. Whatever program you use, never transfer until you have confirmed the exact award seat, because transfers cannot be reversed. Best Airline Programs for Asia Business Class Awards Five programs do most of the work for business class to Asia. Each has a different strength, a different points cost, and a different set of cards that feed it. Here is when to reach for each. Virgin Atlantic Flying Club (to fly ANA) Virgin Atlantic Flying Club is the cheapest well-documented way into ANA business class, the Japanese carrier's celebrated "The Room" suite. Business runs 52,500 points one-way from the U.S. West Coast and 60,000 from the East Coast, and first class ("The Suite") starts at 72,500 points one-way, according to ThriftyTraveler . The draw is accessibility: all five major programs transfer to Flying Club, and most transfers are instant. Two catches to know. You cannot book ANA online through Virgin, so you call Virgin Atlantic and an agent finds the seat, and ANA passes on fuel surcharges of roughly $180 to $350. Even so, a five-figure cash seat for 52,500 points is one of the best deals in the awards world. Turkish Miles&Smiles Turkish Miles&Smiles is the cheapest single program for reaching Asia broadly, pricing business class on Star Alliance partners at about 60,000 miles one-way from the U.S., according to ThriftyTraveler . Star Alliance is a group of airlines that book each other's flights, so those Turkish miles can put you on ANA, EVA Air, or Asiana. Turkish takes transfers from Capital One, Citi, and Bilt, which makes it the go-to if your points are not with Chase or Amex. Two honest caveats: the Turkish website is glitchy and you may need to call to ticket a partner award, and some airlines add fuel surcharges. EVA Air does not, which makes it a favorite here. Air Canada Aeroplan Aeroplan is the most flexible option because it prices by distance and books a long list of Asian carriers, including ANA, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, and Asiana. Business class from North America to Japan or Korea runs 85,000 points one-way, rising to 102,500 for Southeast Asia, as of the June 1, 2026 award chart, according to Upgraded Points . It takes transfers from Chase, Amex, Capital One, and Bilt. The quieter advantage is that many partner awards carry no fuel surcharges, so your out-of-pocket fees stay low even when the mileage price is higher than Virgin or Turkish. Reach for Aeroplan when your dates are firm and you want the widest choice of airlines under one program. Singapore KrisFlyer KrisFlyer is how you fly Singapore Airlines' own business class, consistently rated one of the best in the sky. A saver business seat from the West Coast to Singapore runs about 112,500 miles one-way, according to The Points Guy . "Saver" means the lowest published mileage price, which is also the hardest to find. KrisFlyer takes transfers from Chase, Amex, Capital One, and Citi. It costs more miles than the other programs here, so treat it as the splurge when the experience is the point. Saver space is scarce, so early searching matters more with Singapore than with any other program on this list. ANA Mileage Club (booking ANA direct) If your points are with Amex, you can book ANA through its own program instead. ANA Mileage Club prices round-trip business class to Japan at around 110,000 miles and allows one-way awards on ANA's own flights, according to ANA . American Express is the only flexible-points program that transfers in, alongside Marriott, and that transfer takes a few days. For most people, Virgin Atlantic is the cheaper route onto the exact same ANA plane. Book ANA direct mainly when Virgin shows no space and your Amex points are ready to move well ahead of time. How Many Points Do You Need for Business Class to Asia? Business class to Asia starts around 52,500 to 60,000 points one-way through the cheapest programs, and 85,000 to 112,500 for premium carriers or longer routes. Round-trip commonly lands between 105,000 and 120,000 points. This table compares the main programs for a one-way business class seat: Program Business class cost Cards that transfer Best for Virgin Atlantic (on ANA) From 52,500 one-way Chase, Amex, Capital One, Citi, Bilt Cheapest ANA business, reachable by all Turkish Miles&Smiles ~60,000 one-way Capital One, Citi, Bilt Cheapest single program for broad Asia Air Canada Aeroplan 85,000 one-way (Japan/Korea) Chase, Amex, Capital One, Bilt Flexibility, low surcharges Singapore KrisFlyer ~112,500 one-way Chase, Amex, Capital One, Citi Flying Singapore Airlines itself ANA Mileage Club ~110,000 round-trip Amex only (plus Marriott) Booking ANA direct with Amex points Treat these as starting points, not fixed quotes. Some programs use dynamic and peak-season pricing, so the same route can cost more on busy dates. That is why you search first. Pointhound shows the real points price for your dates across programs, so you compare actual availability instead of award-chart theory. When Does Asia Business Class Award Space Open? Business class award seats to Asia open in two windows: when airlines first load their schedules, about 330 to 355 days out, and again in the final one to three weeks before takeoff as carriers release unsold seats. Both windows reward planning. The early window gives you the widest choice of dates and cities. The late window rewards travelers who can move the moment a seat appears. Here is the honest part. Premium award space to Asia is genuinely scarce. ANA often releases only one or two business class seats per flight, and they get snatched up fast. No search tool can conjure a seat that does not exist, so realistic expectations matter. The biggest lever you control is flexibility: being open on your gateway city, your dates, and which program you use turns a sold-out search into a booking. Watching a route pays off here. Pointhound Flight Alerts track 70,000+ routes and notify you by email or SMS the moment a business class seat opens on a route you want, which is the practical way to catch scarce space at pointhound.com/alerts . How to Book an Asia Business Class Flight With Points, Step by Step Booking an Asia business class award comes down to five steps: confirm the seat, match it to the cheapest program you can reach, transfer your points, book with the airline, and pay the fees in cash. Search the route and dates first. Confirm an actual business class award seat exists on the days you want to fly. A great points price means nothing if no seat is open. Match the seat to a program you can reach. The same ANA flight might be 52,500 points through Virgin Atlantic or 85,000 through Aeroplan. Pick the cheapest program your cards transfer to. Transfer only what you need. Most transfers are instant, but Amex to ANA takes a few days, so move those points early. Never transfer extra "to be safe," because points cannot come back. Book directly with the airline program. Complete the booking on the airline's site, or by phone for ANA-via-Virgin awards. Pay taxes and fuel surcharges in cash. These run from modest to a few hundred dollars depending on the carrier, so check the total before you commit. The order matters more than anything else. Never transfer points before confirming the seat. Every Pointhound search result includes step-by-step booking instructions for that specific award, so you follow a checklist instead of guessing. If you are brand new to this, start with our guide on how to book flights with credit card points . Start With a Search, Not a Transfer The gap between cash and points is widest on the way to Asia, and it is sitting in an account you already have. The mistake most travelers make is transferring points first and hoping a seat appears. Do it the other way around: search the route, find the open business class award, then move exactly what you need. You do not need expert knowledge or a huge balance to fly flat across the Pacific. You need to know which programs fly your route and what a fair price looks like. For the wider premium-cabin playbook, see our guide on cheap business class flights with points , and for another region, how to fly to Europe with points . Pointhound's deal digest sends curated award deals matched to your points and your home airport, so the next strong Asia fare finds you at pointhound.com/digest . Frequently Asked Questions How many points do you need for business class to Asia? Business class to Asia starts around 52,500 to 60,000 points one-way through the cheapest programs, such as Virgin Atlantic on ANA or Turkish Miles&Smiles. Premium carriers or longer routes run 85,000 to 112,500 miles one-way. Round-trip commonly lands between 105,000 and 120,000 points. What is the cheapest way to fly to Asia in business class with points? The cheapest documented path is Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, which books ANA business class from 52,500 points one-way on the West Coast. Turkish Miles&Smiles is close behind at about 60,000 miles one-way and reaches more of Asia on Star Alliance partners like EVA Air. Can you fly ANA business class ("The Room") with points? Yes. The cheapest way is transferring points to Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, which books ANA business class from 52,500 points one-way. You call Virgin to confirm the seat rather than booking online. You can also book ANA directly through ANA Mileage Club using American Express points. Do you pay fuel surcharges on Asia award flights? Sometimes. ANA passes on fuel surcharges of roughly $180 to $350, and Turkish awards on some carriers carry them too. EVA Air and many Star Alliance partners booked through Air Canada Aeroplan have no fuel surcharges, so you pay only modest taxes. Always check the total before transferring. Which credit card is best for business class to Asia? There is no single best card. What matters is that your points transfer to a program that prices your route well. Chase and Amex reach the widest set of Asia programs. Capital One, Citi, and Bilt each feed Turkish or Virgin Atlantic, two of the strongest programs for Asia business class. Key Takeaways A round-trip business class seat to Asia sells for $5,000 to $8,000 or more in cash but books for around 105,000 to 120,000 points, a gap driven by expensive transpacific fares. The cheapest path into ANA business class is Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, from 52,500 points one-way, and all five major programs transfer to it. Turkish Miles&Smiles is the cheapest single program for broad Asia at about 60,000 miles one-way, reachable from Capital One, Citi, and Bilt. Air Canada Aeroplan prices North America to Japan or Korea business at 85,000 points one-way as of June 1, 2026, with no fuel surcharges on many partners. You transfer credit card points into an airline program, then book that airline's seat. Most transfers are instant, but Amex to ANA takes two to four business days. Premium award space to Asia is scarce, so confirm a seat before transferring, and use flight alerts to catch openings on the route you want. Sources Upgraded Points.
